s1.syndrome_frame: intermittent upper abdominal pain with gastrointestinal bleeding
salient_findings: submucosal mass on the lesser curvature of the stomach
key_facts: 3-year history of intermittent upper abdominal pain
episodes of abdominal pain increased in frequency over the past year
dark, tarry stools associated with abdominal pain
submucosal mass on the lesser curvature of the stomach
low-echo lesion with regular, clear margins on endoscopic ultrasound
vascular signal extending from the periphery into the center of the lesion on color Doppler imaging

raw.syndrome_frame: intermittent upper abdominal pain with gastrointestinal bleeding
salient_findings: submucosal mass on the lesser curvature of the stomach
key_facts: 3-year history of intermittent upper abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST)
shortlist.why_kept: submucosal mass with vascular signal on color Doppler imaging

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: submucosal mass with normal overlying mucosa and low-echo lesion on endoscopic ultrasound

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: submucosal mass with rapid growth and gastrointestinal bleeding

shortlist.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
shortlist.why_kept: intermittent gastrointestinal bleeding with normal overlying mucosa

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: submucosal mass with vascular signal on color Doppler imaging and gastrointestinal bleeding

raw.rationale: The presence of a submucosal mass with normal overlying mucosa, a low-echo lesion with regular margins on endoscopic ultrasound, and a vascular signal on color Doppler imaging are consistent with a GIST. The size and location of the mass also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are typically smaller and less likely to cause significant bleeding or anemia.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Leiomyosarcomas are rare and usually have more irregular margins and a higher likelihood of metastasis, which is not indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
rejected.why: Dieulafoy's lesion is a small, superficial lesion that erodes into a vessel, which does not match the description of the large submucosal mass in this case.

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are rare and typically found in the distal stomach or small intestine, and are not as likely to present with the described symptoms and imaging findings.
